description: Paging vectors for the SentiLab view, DRAFT v0.6.1 (view-envelope-0.6.1.md, rules 4 and 5). Generated by `node run-paging-vectors.mjs --write` and checked by `node run-paging-vectors.mjs`. Envelopes keep v0.5's format; the V1 rows come from ../view-envelope-v0.5/vectors-view.json. Scenarios give the polls, what the server does at each, hand-written expectations and the full trace.

rules.cursor_hash: lowercase hex SHA-256 over the raw bytes of rows 0..n-1, each followed by one LF; computed on bytes as received, never on decoded text
rules.request: { cursor, limit } plus cursor_hash for every cursor above 0; never a seq parameter
rules.ok: status 200, body within 256 lines and 4 MiB, x-next-cursor a decimal integer equal to cursor + rows returned, and x-cursor-hash equal to the client's own hash of all rows it would then hold
rules.failures: transport: no response, a status other than 200, 400, 404, 409, 413 or 501, or a body over the caps; paging_error: a bad x-next-cursor, more rows than the requested limit, a non-empty body that doesn't end with LF, or a bad x-cursor-hash; stream_replaced: 409; row_too_large: 413; paging_unsupported: 400, 404 or 501. A failed poll keeps no rows and never resets the cursor; stream_replaced, row_too_large and paging_unsupported are terminal: no more requests until a manual reload
rules.label: a failed latest poll shows "STALE · <reason>" (transport, paging error, stream replaced, row too large, paging unsupported); otherwise, if K is below the highest value it has reached or anything follows the projectable prefix (the board is frozen), "STALE · chain broken" at once; otherwise the v0.5 progress tracker, fed only with valid pages, gives LIVE or STALE
rules.bytes_to_rows: split raw bytes on LF (0x0A) only; a trailing LF doesn't start a row; decode each row on its own as strict UTF-8 keeping any BOM (TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true })); a row that isn't valid UTF-8 is malformed (invalid_utf8), a row starting with a BOM is malformed (not_json, since JSON.parse rejects it), and the page continues; the same for replay files, except that a replay file's last line may lack its LF and still counts as a row; the hash never sees decoded text
rules.server: 400 for a cursor or limit outside the allowed range; 409 for a cursor beyond the end, or above 0 without a cursor_hash or with one that doesn't match; 413, with no body and no cursor headers, when the row at the cursor plus its LF is over 4 MiB; otherwise as many whole rows, each with its LF, as fit within 4 MiB, up to limit, with x-next-cursor, x-has-more and x-cursor-hash; never a 200 over 4 MiB
rules.complete_rows: the log is its complete, LF-terminated rows (logRowsFromFile); a tail with no LF yet is neither served, counted nor hashed until its LF is written
rules.rows: text rows are UTF-8; base64 rows are raw bytes; fill rows are `bytes` copies of `fill`. In logs and bodies, ["id", n] means n copies
rules.server_behaviors: log: servePage() over that log; headers: overrides, null removes; tamper: replace that log row in the body only; page: exactly those rows after the log, consistent headers, no limit; status + legacy: that status for cursor requests, and a legacy 200 page (rows with seq > after, no paging headers) if a request carries after; strip_final_lf: drop the body's final LF; network_error: no response

label_cases.name: K at its high, nothing after the prefix, progress 1 s ago: LIVE
a refused row after the prefix, K still at its high: STALE · chain broken
K below its high on its own: STALE · chain broken
K below its high and the board frozen: STALE · chain broken
a failed latest poll shows its own reason first, even on a frozen board
not frozen, but no progress for 61 s: STALE

bytes_to_rows.name: a trailing LF ends the last row and doesn't start a new one
no trailing LF: the last row is still a row
a blank line in the middle is a row
an empty body has no rows
a lone LF is one blank row
only LF splits: a CR stays in the row
invalid UTF-8 (FF) is no text, and the next row still decodes
an overlong encoding (C0 AF) is not valid UTF-8
an encoded surrogate (ED A0 80) is not valid UTF-8

cursor_hash_cases.name: no rows: the SHA-256 of nothing
one row {}: the SHA-256 of {} and LF
a row with invalid UTF-8 is hashed as received; decoding first would give a different hash

server_logs.log600: row i (0 to 599) is the ASCII text {"row":i}, except when i % 100 is 7: then it is {"row":i,"raw":" followed by the bytes FF FE and then "}

server_files.c14-tail: the rows {"row":0} to {"row":4}, each followed by LF, then {"row":5} with no LF
server_files.c14-done: the rows {"row":0} to {"row":5}, each followed by LF

server_cases.name: cursor 0, limit 256: rows 0 to 255
cursor 256 with the hash of rows 0..255: rows 256 to 511
cursor 512: the last 88 rows, no more
cursor 600 (the end): 0 rows, no more
cursor 601 (beyond the end): 409
a stale cursor_hash (from a log whose row 3 differs): 409
a cursor above 0 without cursor_hash: 409
cursor 0, limit 1
limit 0: 400
limit 257: 400
cursor -1: 400
rows of 65,535 bytes: a page stops at 64 rows, exactly 4 MiB
a first row of 4,194,304 bytes (4,194,305 with its LF): 413, no body, no cursor headers
65 rows of 65,535 bytes: whole rows up to exactly 4 MiB (64 rows), the 65th left for the next page
the next page holds the deferred 65th row
a file whose last row has no LF: only the 5 complete rows are served and hashed
cursor 5 on that file: 0 rows; the tail is not served
cursor 6 on that file is beyond the end: 409 (the tail is not counted)
once the LF lands, cursor 5 with the earlier hash gets the sixth row
after the LF, all 6 rows from cursor 0

scenarios.name: C2 truncated log: the log shrinks to 5 rows, so cursor 11 is beyond its end; 409, stream replaced, the prefix is kept, no reset, no more requests

C4 rows, not envelopes: a byte-identical duplicate, a non-JSON row and a row with invalid UTF-8 each advance the cursor by one; the result equals verifying the same rows as one file

C6c a 400 on the cursor parameters is no cursor support too

C8b replaced log that is longer (row 5 differs, two rows added): the old cursor_hash gets 409, stream replaced, the prefix is kept
C9 hash mismatch: a page whose row 9 was altered in transit, then a page with no x-cursor-hash; each is a paging error and its rows are not kept
C10 bytes to rows: one page holding a BOM-prefixed copy of seq 1 and a row of invalid UTF-8; both are malformed, the 11 other rows verify, and the cursor hash covers the raw bytes of all 13
